questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the benefits of the retired President of India?
A. The former President of India will also be entitled to a monthly pension of ₹2.5 lakh.
B. He/She is entitled to a secretarial staff comprising a private secretary, a personal assistant, an additional private secretary, two peons, and office expenses up to ₹1 lakh per annum.
C. He/She is also entitled to free highest-class travel anywhere in India, accompanied by one person, by rail, air, or steamer.

भारत के सेवानिवृत्त राष्ट्रपति के लाभों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
A. भारत के पूर्व राष्ट्रपति भी ₹2.5 लाख की मासिक पेंशन के हकदार होंगे।
B. वह एक सचिवीय स्टाफ का हकदार है जिसमें एक निजी सचिव, एक निजी सहायक, एक अतिरिक्त निजी सचिव, दो चपरासी और प्रति वर्ष ₹1 लाख तक का कार्यालय व्यय शामिल है।
C. वह भारत में कहीं भी, एक व्यक्ति के साथ, रेल, हवाई या स्टीमर द्वारा निःशुल्क उच्चतम श्रेणी की यात्रा का भी हकदार है।
questions.solution:
Regarding the benefits of a retired President, all three statements are correct.
  • Pension: Under the President's Emoluments and Pension Act, they receive a monthly pension of ₹2.5 lakh (50% of the last drawn salary).
  • Secretarial Help: They are provided with secretarial staff and office expenses up to ₹1 lakh per annum.
  • Travel: They enjoy free highest-class travel (rail, air, or steamer) across India with one companion.

questions.question: In which year was the Estimates Committee constituted for the first time in India?
questions.solution:
The Estimates Committee was constituted for the first time in 1950.
  • Recommendation: It was established on the recommendation of John Mathai, the then Finance Minister.
  • Function: It examines the estimates included in the budget and suggests 'economies' in public expenditure.
  • Membership: It consists of 30 members, all of whom are elected solely from the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following is constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Article 280 of the Constitution provides for the establishment of the Finance Commission.
  • Appointment: It is constituted by the President of India every five years or earlier.
  • Role: Its primary duty is to recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India consists of the idea of a Welfare State?
questions.solution:
The idea of a Welfare State is primarily enshrined in the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
  • Objective: Found in Part IV, these principles direct the state to ensure social, economic, and political justice.
  • Purpose: Unlike a police state, a welfare state works toward the betterment of all citizens through health, education, and social security.

questions.question:
With the 2022 amendments to the Indian Constitution, which of the following communities have been granted the Scheduled Tribes status by the Government of India?
A. Narikoravan community
B. Hattee community
C. Kadu Kuruba community
D. Kapu community
questions.solution:
Following the 2022 amendments, the Narikoravan (Tamil Nadu), Hattee (Himachal Pradesh), and Kadu Kuruba (Karnataka) communities were granted Scheduled Tribe (ST) status.
  • Process: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Amendment) Bills were passed to include these communities.
  • Excluded: The Kapu community (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana) was not part of this specific ST status granting group in 2022.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India empowers a high court to issue a writ?
questions.solution:
Article 226 empowers a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.
  • Comparison: While Article 32 gives similar powers to the Supreme Court, the writ jurisdiction of the High Court is wider because it can issue writs for ordinary legal rights as well.
  • Types: It can issue Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.

questions.question: In India, which of the following bills CANNOT be introduced in the Rajya Sabha?
questions.option_3: Both constitutional amendment and ordinary bills
questions.solution:
In India, a Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
  • Exclusive Power: According to Article 109, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha with the recommendation of the President.
  • Rajya Sabha Role: The Upper House can only suggest recommendations within 14 days, which the Lok Sabha may or may not accept.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India lays down that an Indian citizen has the right to use any restaurant, road or public place?
questions.solution:
Article 15(2) specifically states that no citizen shall be subject to any disability or restriction regarding access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment.
  • Public Utilities: It also covers the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads, and places of public resort maintained by State funds.
  • Anti-Discrimination: This is a crucial provision against social exclusion and untouchability.

questions.question: In India, who among the following is responsible for auditing all receipts and expenditure of the Union and State governments?
questions.solution:
The Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG) of India is responsible for auditing all receipts and expenditures of both the Union and State governments.
  • Guardian: Known as the 'Guardian of the Public Purse,' the CAG ensures that money is spent as authorized by Parliament.
  • Reporting: The CAG submits audit reports to the President (for the Union) and Governors (for States).

questions.question: How many types of writs can be issued under Article 32 and 226 of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Both the Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226) can issue five types of writs.
  • The Five Writs: 1. Habeas Corpus, 2. Mandamus, 3. Prohibition, 4. Certiorari, and 5. Quo Warranto.
  • Constitutional Remedies: These writs are the primary tools for the judicial protection of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Article 148 of the Constitution of India provides for an independent office of the ________.
questions.option_3: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.solution:
Article 148 provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG).
  • Independence: To ensure impartiality, the CAG is appointed by the President but can only be removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court Judge.
  • Tenure: The CAG holds office for a term of 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

questions.question: In India, who appoints the Advocate General of a State?
questions.solution:
The Governor of the State appoints the Advocate General for that State.
  • Qualification: A person must be qualified to be appointed as a High Court Judge to hold this post.
  • Role: He/She is the highest law officer in the State, providing legal advice to the state government.

questions.question: When was the None of the Above (NOTA) ballot option first implemented in India?
questions.solution:
The None of the Above (NOTA) option was first implemented in India in 2013.
  • Judgement: This followed a Supreme Court ruling in the PUCL vs. Union of India case.
  • Implementation: It was first used in the 2013 assembly elections in five states (Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Delhi).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles mentions about a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India?
questions.solution:
Article 44 of the DPSP mentions that the State shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout India.
  • Concept: UCC aims to replace personal laws based on religion with a common set of laws governing marriage, divorce, and inheritance.
  • Current Status: As of now, it remains a directive and is not legally enforceable, except in the state of Goa.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Supreme Court judgement on validity of 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act?
A. The Supreme Court of India’s Constitutional Bench for this case consisted of 5 judges.
B. The Constitutional Bench upholds the 10% of EWS reservation with 3-2 majority.
C. As per the Supreme Court judgement, the 103rd Constitutional Amendment is valid although it is violating the Basic Structure of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution:
Statements A and B regarding the 103rd Amendment Act (EWS Reservation) are correct.
  • Bench: The case was heard by a 5-judge Constitutional Bench.
  • Verdict: The bench upheld the 10% reservation for EWS with a 3-2 majority.
  • Incorrect: Statement C is wrong; the Supreme Court ruled that the amendment does NOT violate the Basic Structure of the Constitution.
